prize_parts.citation: for developing methods to estimate demand and competition in differentiated-product markets with endogenous prices, and models of dynamic industries, which transformed empirical industrial organisation and the measurement of market power and welfare

statement.case_for: My configuration is unchanged from round 1: B001 as a single achievement, credited to Pakes, Berry and Levinsohn, with a method-level citation. The exchange has not moved me on the merits, but it has made the unit of the prize clearer. The achievement is the ability to recover substitution patterns, markups and welfare from market data when prices are endogenous and products are differentiated. The dynamic-industry framework is supporting context for that. On the chair's toolkit-versus-discovery question, my criterion is whether a contribution (a) created a measurement capability that was not available before, (b) allowed counterfactuals that earlier reduced-form work could not answer, (c) was adopted in institutional practice, and (d) spread beyond its home field. From the evidence members cite, B001 meets all four. Merger review and regulatory analysis are the institutional-practice case, and trade, health and environmental economics are the spread. The core is about thirty years old, so the sensitivities are documented and the question of maturity is settled. Compact credit also helps: the 1995 paper has three authors, and the three-laureate cap fits it without splitting the paper. I come from market design, where moving from theory to institutional practice is the test I would apply to any candidate. I would apply the same test to B050, B013 and B002. On the single-achievement question Stromberg raised, I prefer one part. A second part would either add a person beyond the three already needed here or force a weaker pairing, and I see no second achievement that improves the citation.
statement.case_against: The strongest reservation remains the third name and the unit of the prize. Excluding Bresnahan leaves out the founder of the new empirical IO programme, and the method-level citation does not claim his contribution. A three-name cap also leaves out Reiss, Benkard and Levin. The toolkit-versus-discovery weighting is a genuine difference in judgement, and the Committee may reasonably reach a different view. Applied structural results are sensitive to functional form, instrument choice and numerical implementation, and the claim that these problems are largely addressed rests on members' background knowledge, mine included. I would want documented merger-review cases and replication studies to confirm it, and I cannot supply them here. The citation should be worded so that it does not imply that every applied estimate is robust.

responses.point: Krusell proposes Pakes, Berry and Bresnahan. He argues that Bresnahan's market-power measurement and new empirical IO supplied the question the later tools answered, he calls the Levinsohn/Bresnahan choice a close call, and he says a Levinsohn version would not be a scientific error.
responses.response: I take his concession and the chair's framing question as the right way to settle this, because we share the same method. The choice is a choice of citation, not a verdict on merit. A method-level citation (demand with endogenous prices plus dynamic industries) points to Levinsohn as co-author of the defining paper, and dropping him while keeping Berry splits a three-author result. A programme-level citation points to Bresnahan, but that is a wider and more diffusely attributed prize. I would keep the method-level framing and Levinsohn, and I would accept Bresnahan only with a programme-level rewording that does not describe the BLP paper itself as the achievement. I accept his point that the dynamic-games and production-function strands are Pakes's, and the citation should treat them as context and not claim all of them.

responses.point: Hassler, as chair and a B001 supporter, argues that the unit should be defined narrowly as demand and competition estimation plus the dynamic-industry framework. He warns that adding production-function work or entry models would blur the unit and reopen attribution. He also keeps B002 to the clean Kiyotaki-Moore pair.
responses.response: I agree with the narrow unit, and I have drafted the citation accordingly. Widening it to cover production functions, entry and the whole empirical-IO agenda would bring back exactly the seven-name attribution problem that makes the compact version attractive. I also carry over his B002 point, as in round 1. If the Committee turns to B002, it should be the Kiyotaki-Moore pair without Gertler, and I would not carry Gertler into that alternative. I add one caution to his own case. The compactness of the BLP credit does not by itself answer the toolkit-versus-discovery question, so I rely on the four-part test above and not on the attribution argument alone.

responses.point: Hjalmarsson keeps B013 first with Autor, Katz and Hanson. She argues it has the cleanest link between evidence and framework and that the China-shock designs test a specific mechanism. She says B001 is the strongest alternative and calls it mostly a toolkit prize, a difference in judgement and not a merit gap she can establish.
responses.response: I accept that this is a difference in judgement, and I accept that the China-shock designs test a mechanism and are not merely descriptive. I still keep B013 below B001, for two reasons that are about credit and settledness. The Committee would have to decide whether it is crediting the task or skill-demand framework or the trade-shock evidence. Under the three-name cap that decision leaves out either Katz or Dorn, and the Committee has no rule to make that choice. The long-run magnitudes of the shock are also still being refined. Her point that a toolkit and a discovery are weighed differently is why I stated my four-part test openly. On that test B001 meets the criteria, and I would not claim B013 fails them, only that its credit boundary is less settled today.

responses.point: Boppart keeps B050 first with Melitz and Helpman. He argues that a tight firm-heterogeneity citation can exclude Helpman's B021 political-economy work, and he accepts that Bernard, Eaton, Jensen and Kortum, and Redding, are real attribution costs. He treats B001 as a close alternative and says the Bresnahan versus Levinsohn choice is unsettled.
responses.response: His answer on B021 is a fair reply to my round 1 concern: a citation tied to selection and reallocation does keep Helpman's protection-for-sale work out of scope. I therefore weigh that objection less than before, and B050 remains my first alternative. The remaining cost is the one he concedes, the parallel contributors outside the two-name design, and I would not treat the ballot entry as resolving it. I also disagree gently with his remark that B001's attribution is unsettled. The third name is contested, but the Pakes-Berry core and the BLP paper are not. I would put the dispute at the boundary of the credit and not at its centre. On the 2008 prize, his distinction between increasing-returns trade theory and firm heterogeneity is persuasive to me as a substantive point. It does not close the Committee's question about appetite for a second trade award.

uncertainties: Whether the Committee prefers a method-level citation with Levinsohn or a programme-level citation with Bresnahan, and whether Pakes's dynamic-games and production-function work should be claimed in the citation or only mentioned as context.

Whether the Committee will weigh a measurement-and-methods contribution the same as a substantive finding. I applied a four-part test (new measurement capability, new counterfactuals, institutional adoption, spread beyond the field), but the test is my own judgement and the Committee may weigh it differently.

Which of the documented sensitivities (numerical implementation, instrument choice, functional form) would change a merger-review or welfare conclusion in practice. This could be settled with documented cases and replication studies, which I do not have.
How the Committee would resolve attribution on B050 (Redding and the outside group) and B013 (Katz versus Dorn) if it moved away from B001, and whether Gertler would be added to a B002 pair.
Citation counts, regulatory-adoption claims and the status of the numerical and identification problems all rest on my background knowledge and have not been independently verified.
statement.conflict_note: Updated after round 1: none apparent from the supplied profile. Neither my listed co-authors (Svensson, Ehlers, Erlanson, Martinello, Teytelboym, Trapp, Biró) nor my institutional ties include Pakes, Berry, Levinsohn or Bresnahan on B001, Melitz or Helpman on B050, or Kiyotaki or Moore on B002. My market-design work, the Swedish and Scandiatransplant kidney exchange programmes and the school-choice advice are not connected to those candidates. I am an affiliate of SSE alongside committee colleagues Dreber Almenberg, Friberg and Strömberg, which is a link between committee members and not to a candidate. I gave the 2020 presentation speech, but a speech for the Academy does not establish a personal preference and I do not treat it as a conflict. These disclosures are not adjudicated.
